title: Cold rebuild: the time-box planner
summary: Rebuild the largest-remainder time-box planner from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You wrote **An interview time-box planner** in *Running the interview*. Write it
again from an **empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution. The tests are the ones you passed.
The planner is small, but the habit behind it is the one that matters: decide the time boxes before the clock
starts, and keep them. If you get stuck, go back to the lesson and try again tomorrow.

steps.prompt: Twenty minutes into a 45-minute interview you are still on the high-level design. Put what you do next in order.
lines: Say where you are: "I'm a few minutes over on the design; let me wrap this part up"
Finish the main read and write paths in a sentence each
Ask which part the interviewer wants to go deep on
Keep the last five minutes for bottlenecks and failure modes
steps.explain: Naming the overrun and asking the interviewer to choose the deep dive turns a time problem into a sign that you can run a meeting.

steps.title: Cold rebuild: the time-box planner
prompt: From memory: write `int[] TimeBoxes(int totalMinutes, int[] weights)` that splits `totalMinutes` across the
phases in proportion to `weights`, in whole minutes that add up exactly to `totalMinutes`, by the largest
remainder method (integer shares first; the leftover minutes go one each to the largest remainders, the
earlier phase first on a tie). Empty weights or a sum of 0 or less throw `ArgumentException`.
